items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I still study, trying to find out what's going on, along with Beethoven and Mozart

ctx.x: As if it were engraved in stone.

Yeah. And missing the real point of the thing possibly in the process, so that all you're doing is imitating--or you're following the rules set down by almost everyone else than Beethoven, something else of the period that Beethoven wrote it, the cultural feel of that period. Subsequent cultures don't really respond to that.

His music, as played by the Julliard quartet, and especially the (inaudible) quartet, it roared--Beethoven roared. Such a magnificent great man. (Inaudible). If you can bring a sense of enduring or substance to a contemporary piece (inaudible).
